persona.name: Daisuke Wakamiya

occupation.title: Owner and Creative Director
occupation.organization: A 5-person web design studio (goudou kaisha) in Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto
occupation.description: Founded the studio at 29 after agency years in Osaka. Handles client pitches, project direction, and — because there is no one else — accounting, HR, and IT. About 8 meetings a week, mostly client kickoffs and reviews, half over video. Every tool decision is his alone, and every subscription is money out of a margin he watches obsessively.

persona.education: Design degree from Kyoto Seika University; self-taught in front-end development and, painfully, in bookkeeping.
long_term_goals: Grow to eight people without losing the studio's character
Land a flagship client in traditional crafts e-commerce
Stop being the studio's accountant by 37
Renovate the machiya his studio rents the first floor of
persona.style: Soft-spoken with the unhurried Kyoto cadence, letting silences do work in negotiations. Explains design decisions with concrete metaphors and hates buzzwords — says 'DX' with visible quotation marks. With his small team he is direct and warm; with tools and vendors he is courteous, cheap, and hard to close.

traits: Protective of his small team's time

interests: Whether AI notes can replace the junior he can't afford to assign to minutes
Client-meeting records as protection in scope disputes
Typography and traditional Kyoto color palettes
likes: Tools priced for five people, not five hundred
Annual plans with a real discount
Clients who decide things in the meeting
dislikes: Per-user pricing that punishes small teams
Enterprise sales calls for a 5-person company
Invoices in dollars that fluctuate with the exchange rate

beliefs: A written record has saved him from two unpaid scope disputes; memory is not a business tool
Every recurring cost must displace a real hour of labor
Small studios survive on judgment, not headcount
skills: Saying no to bad projects politely

general: Assigns a junior designer to take notes in client meetings, feels guilty about it
Keeps a 'tools considered and rejected' note with reasons and prices
Reviews all subscriptions every January and cancels at least one
Records important client calls locally after a dispute in 2024

morning: 7:00 wake, hand-drip coffee ritual, walks to the studio
Quiet design work 8:30-10:30 before anyone arrives
workday: Client meetings late morning and afternoon
Evenings: quotes, invoices, and the accounting he resents
evening: Kamogawa run three evenings a week
Cooks simply, reads design books or watches NBA clips
weekend: Saturday client work when deadlines demand
Sunday temple flea markets and coffee roasting experiments

health.physical: Runner-fit; recurring wrist strain from mouse work he manages with a brace.
health.mental: Cash-flow anxiety comes in waves at month-end; running and roasting are his stated coping mechanisms, and they mostly work.

relationships.name: Kaori Wakamiya
relationships.description: A curator at a Kyoto textile museum; his sanity check on both design taste and business risks.

relationships.name: Ippei
relationships.description: Loyal and overworked; the unofficial minutes-taker whose design hours Daisuke wants back.
